items.text: Nemáš chuť ísť zajtra korčuľovať? = Do you fancy going skating tomorrow?
items.picture: Split picture of a phone call. Left: Tomáš, a pair of ice skates slung over his shoulder, phones cheerfully from a snowy street. Right: in the dorm room, Emma, in bed with a blanket round her and a box of tissues beside her, answers, looking miserable.

items.text: Prosím? — Ahoj, Emma, tu je Tomáš. Nemáš chuť ísť zajtra korčuľovať? Emma's phone rings. What does Tomáš want?
Your phone rings. How can you answer it?
Ako sa cítiš? = How are you feeling?
Prechladla som. = I've caught a cold. (a woman speaking)
Mám nádchu. = I've got a runny nose.
items.picture: Emma, wrapped in a blanket at her desk in the dorm room, blows her red nose into a tissue; crumpled tissues pile up beside her.

items.text: Kašlem. = I've got a cough.
items.picture: Emma, sitting up in bed in the dorm room, coughs hard into her elbow, her eyes screwed shut.

items.text: Vyzeráš zle. = You look ill.
items.picture: Lucia, just home, her bag still on her shoulder, stops in the doorway of the dorm room and looks at Emma with concern: Emma, huddled on her bed in a blanket, is pale as a sheet, with dark rings under her eyes.

items.text: Si bledá. = You're pale. (to a woman)
teplota = temperature
items.picture: In the dorm room, Emma, sitting up in bed, squints at the thermometer she has just taken from under her arm; Lucia leans over to look too.

items.text: Mám teplotu tridsaťosem stupňov. Emma looks at the thermometer. What does she say?
med = honey
sestrička = nurse
items.picture: At the doctor's surgery, the nurse opens the door of the consulting room and calls in the next patient; in the waiting room, Emma, wrapped in her scarf, gets up from her chair.

items.text: preukaz poistenca = health insurance card
items.picture: At the nurse's desk in the doctor's surgery, Emma hands over her blue European health insurance card; the nurse holds out her hand for it, smiling.

items.text: Dobrý deň. Máte preukaz poistenca? What does the nurse want to see?
čakáreň = waiting room
items.picture: The waiting room of the doctor's surgery: chairs along the walls, a coat stand, a window. The pensioner waits with his stick, a young mother holds a coughing toddler on her knee, and Emma, in her scarf, sniffles into a tissue.

items.text: Ďalší, prosím! = Next, please!
The nurse opens the door to call in the next patient. What does she say?
lekár a pacient = doctor and patient
Čo vám je? = What's the matter?
Dýchajte zhlboka. = Breathe deeply.
items.picture: In the doctor's surgery, Emma sits on the edge of the examination couch in her white T-shirt and takes a deep breath, eyes closed; the doctor listens to her back through her stethoscope.

items.text: Ukážte mi hrdlo. = Show me your throat.
items.picture: In the doctor's surgery, Emma opens her mouth wide to say ah; the doctor, holding a wooden spatula, shines a small torch into her throat.

items.text: angína = tonsillitis, strep throat
Nie je to zápal pľúc, je to angína. What does the doctor say?
Mám chrípku. = I've got flu.
antibiotiká = antibiotics
Pite veľa tekutín. = Drink plenty of fluids.
items.picture: Emma, in bed in the dorm room, drinks a big glass of water; on her bedside table stand a full jug of water, a teapot and a bottle of juice.

items.text: lekárnička = pharmacist (a woman)
items.picture: A pharmacy: shelves of medicine boxes and a glass cabinet behind the counter. The pharmacist takes Emma's prescription across the counter and reads it over her half-moon glasses.

items.text: na recept, bez receptu = on prescription, over the counter
Antibiotiká sú na recept. What does the pharmacist say?
tabletka = tablet, pill
items.picture: Close up at Emma's desk: Emma presses a small white tablet out of a blister strip into her palm; the opened pack and a glass of water stand beside it.

items.text: trikrát denne = three times a day
items.picture: Three small scenes of one day, side by side, in the dorm room: in the morning, the sun rising in the window; at midday, the sun high; at night, the moon in the window. Each time Emma takes a tablet with a glass of water.

items.text: The pharmacist says: Užívajte dve tabletky dvakrát denne. How many tablets a day is that?
balenie = pack, packet
V jednom balení je dvadsať tabletiek. What does this tell you?
sirup proti kašľu = cough syrup
kvapky do nosa = nose drops
items.picture: At the mirror in the dorm bathroom, Emma tips her head back and squeezes drops from a small bottle into her nose.

items.text: Máte niečo proti nádche? What is Emma asking for?
Čo mi odporúčate? = What do you recommend?
items.picture: At the pharmacy counter, Emma, sniffling, asks the pharmacist's advice; the pharmacist holds up a bottle of cough syrup, recommending it.

items.text: vitamíny = vitamins
To si nemôžem dovoliť. = I can't afford that.
Nechaj tak, ja to zaplatím. = Leave it, I'll pay.
items.picture: At the pharmacy counter, Emma, a big jar of vitamins in her hand, winces as she looks into her nearly empty purse; Lucia, beside her, waves Emma's purse away and holds her own card to the card reader, while the pharmacist smiles.

items.text: Lucia wants to pay for Emma's vitamins. What does she say?
lyžovačka = skiing trip
Spadol som. = I fell. (a man speaking)
Zlomil som si ruku. = I've broken my arm. (a man speaking)
items.picture: On a snowy ski slope in the mountains, Marek sits in the snow after a fall, his skis tangled, clutching his arm and wincing with pain; Tomáš skids to a stop beside him.

items.text: Zavolaj sanitku! = Call an ambulance!
items.picture: On the ski slope, Tomáš kneels in the snow beside Marek, who lies holding his arm, and phones urgently for an ambulance; other skiers stop to look.

items.text: Marek can't get up. Which number does Tomáš call?
nemocnica = hospital
items.picture: An ambulance with its blue lights flashing pulls up at the A&E entrance of a big hospital; paramedics help Marek out, his arm strapped to his chest, and Tomáš follows. Through the glass doors: a waiting area with rows of plastic chairs.

items.text: pohotovosť = A&E, emergency service
Kde vás bolí? = Where does it hurt?
items.picture: In the hospital's bright treatment room, Veronika asks Marek gently where it hurts; Marek, sitting on the couch, points to his forearm, wincing.

items.text: Dobrý deň, volám sa Veronika, som lekárka. Kde vás bolí? Who is talking to Marek at A&E?
zlomenina = fracture, break
items.picture: In the hospital's treatment room, Veronika points to the X-ray of Marek's forearm on the screen, where the bone is clearly broken; Marek stares at it in dismay.

items.text: sadra = plaster cast
items.picture: In the hospital's treatment room, Veronika smooths the last of a white plaster cast round Marek's arm, from his hand to his elbow, and wags a finger at him with a smile as he protests that he has to get back to work.

items.text: byť na PN-ke = to be on sick leave
items.picture: A weekday morning in Marek's living room: Marek, his arm in plaster, slumps on the sofa in his red flannel shirt, scowling and bored, a cookery show on the TV.

items.text: Šesť týždňov budete na PN-ke. What does Veronika tell Marek?
Práca vám neutečie. = Work can wait.
Som nahnevaný. Marek can't cook for six weeks. What does he mean?
Musíte si oddýchnuť. Práca vám neutečie. What does Veronika tell Marek before he goes home?
hlava a krk = head and neck
items.picture: At his laptop in his untidy office, Tomáš tilts his head to one side and rubs the back of his stiff neck.

items.text: rameno a ruka = shoulder and arm
items.picture: In Marek's living room, Marek shows Lucia where it hurts: he touches his shoulder with his good hand; his other arm, in a white plaster cast, rests in a sling.

items.text: chrbát a brucho = back and stomach
items.picture: Two halves. Left: Tomáš, stiff after the skiing trip, bends forward with a hand pressed to his aching back. Right: Lucia curls up on the sofa clutching her stomach, a half-eaten box of chocolates beside her.

items.text: noha a koleno = leg and knee
srdce = heart
items.picture: In a hospital corridor, Marek, his arm in plaster, presses his good hand to his heart and gazes dreamily after Veronika as she walks away.

items.text: tvár = face
items.picture: A close-up of Veronika's face at the hospital, smiling warmly.

items.text: oči a uši = eyes and ears
items.picture: In the Šimkos' living room, Samko pulls a funny face at Lucia: he pulls his ears out to the sides with his fingers and opens his eyes as wide as they will go; Lucia laughs.

items.text: nos a ústa = nose and mouth
items.picture: In the snowy front garden of the Šimkos' house, Samko finishes a snowman's face: he pushes in a carrot for its nose and a curved row of small pebbles for its smiling mouth.

items.text: Marek má krátke kučeravé vlasy. What does Marek look like?
zubár = dentist
items.picture: At the dentist's: Emma lies back in the big dentist's chair with her mouth wide open and her eyes wide; the dentist, a man in a white tunic with a mask under his chin, leans over her with a small mirror.

items.text: všeobecný lekár = GP, family doctor
Nevidím dobre. = I can't see well.
items.picture: In the Šimkos' kitchen, babka Helena tries to thread a needle, holding it at arm's length and squinting; she can't see the eye of it. Her glasses lie on the table beside her.

items.text: bolesť = pain, ache
Pán Kováč says: Nepočujem dobre. Which doctor should he see?
items.picture: At the porter's lodge, Emma says something through the window; pán Kováč leans towards her, cupping a hand behind his ear and frowning: he can't hear well.

items.text: Užívajte jednu tabletku trikrát denne. Listen. How often should you take the tablet?
